items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged the Houthis to cease attacks, warning that a recent strike on a Chinese-flagged Saudi fuel ship could draw China into the conflict.
items.rawSummary: Walter Reed continues to treat U.S. personnel wounded in the Iran conflict as the U.S. escalates military operations, threatens heavier strikes, and faces broadening diplomatic and security challenges.
items.analysis: Walter Reed has treated nearly 100 U.S. personnel wounded in the Iran conflict over the past two weeks, with a 96% return-to-duty rate. The broader conflict reached a new inflection point after President Trump said he ordered U.S. forces to 'open the gates of hell' on Iran, and Kan News reported the U.S. has informed Israel it plans to escalate strikes, including using heavy bombers for the first time in the campaign. Earlier in the day, Axios reported Trump was weighing a ceasefire or a large-scale joint campaign with Israel, but Secretary of State Marco Rubio now says Iran is not willing to reach an agreement, warning of a 'head for an eye' approach and asserting the U.S. kept its end of a prior deal. Rubio also addressed Houthi attacks on shipping, warning that a recent strike on a Chinese-flagged Saudi fuel vessel risks drawing China into the conflict and urged the Houthis to de-escalate. The war's official cost has reached $37.5 billion, with the administration seeking an additional $67 billion from Congress, while domestic support has eroded among Trump's base amid rising gas prices and military casualties. Diplomatic coordination also surfaced as Axios reported Mossad chief Roman Gofman held talks in Washington two weeks ago on Iran policy with CIA Director John Ratcliffe and White House officials. Reuters reported that U.S. intelligence analysts are investigating whether Russia provided targeting intelligence or upgraded drone technology to Iran, following strikes that hit CIA facilities in Riyadh and eastern Iraq. On the legislative front, the House passed an NDAA amendment blocking transgender medical procedures under TRICARE, a policy that would affect military medical facilities like Walter Reed, and separately passed a $1.15 trillion defense bill with $60 billion in additional war-related spending, heading to the Senate amid Democratic opposition over the unauthorized conflict. Declassified White House documents seeking to show Chinese election meddling instead exposed extensive Russian interference operations, Clash Report revealed. The U.S. issued a global advisory warning that diplomatic facilities, businesses, and other American institutions could face threats worldwide amid rising tensions.

items.title: Manila, Philippines: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov during the ASEAN summit in Manila.
items.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov during the ASEAN summit in Manila.
items.rawSummary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov met in Manila during the ASEAN summit, against a backdrop of U.S. concerns about Russia potentially providing targeting data to Iran.
items.analysis: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN Ministerial Conference, amid growing concern among U.S. decision-makers that Russia is supplying Iran with targeting data for American bases and infrastructure across the Middle East. The encounter marked a rare high-level diplomatic contact between the two countries at a time of heightened tensions. It remained unclear whether the issue of alleged Russian intelligence sharing with Iran was addressed, or if the talks focused on broader bilateral or regional matters.

items.title: Islamabad, Pakistan: Pakistan requests a $10 billion exchange stabilization facility from the U.S. Treasury following its diplomatic mediation in the Iran conflict.
items.description: Pakistan requests a $10 billion exchange stabilization facility from the U.S. Treasury following its diplomatic mediation in the Iran conflict.
items.rawSummary: Pakistan threatened military action against Yemen's Ansarallah over Red Sea or Saudi attacks while simultaneously pursuing a $10 billion U.S. financial backstop following its mediation in the Iran conflict.
items.analysis: Pakistan declared that any attack by Yemen's Ansarallah on Pakistani vessels in the Red Sea or on Saudi Arabia would be treated as a threat to its national security, warning of a military response. The statement signals Islamabad's readiness to involve itself in a regional conflict already disrupting key maritime routes and reflects a deepening alignment with Saudi security concerns. Separately, Pakistan has requested a $10 billion exchange stabilization facility from the U.S. Treasury, seeking to bolster foreign reserves, stabilize the rupee, and reduce reliance on IMF loans. The request follows Pakistan's diplomatic mediation during the Iran conflict, with Islamabad hoping its role will translate into stronger economic ties with Washington. No decision on the facility has been announced.

items.title: Muscat, Oman, Oman: Oman's Foreign Minister discussed regional issues including the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen with his Pakistani counterpart.
items.description: Oman's Foreign Minister discussed regional issues including the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen with his Pakistani counterpart.
items.rawSummary: Oman is pursuing diplomacy to revive Yemen's political process, coordinating with Saudi Arabia, Yemeni parties, the UN, and Pakistan, while raising concerns about maritime security in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz.
items.analysis: Oman's foreign ministry announced it is coordinating with Saudi Arabia, Yemeni parties, and the UN envoy to restore the political process in Yemen, and cautioned against any escalation threatening freedom of navigation in the Red Sea. The foreign minister subsequently discussed regional issues, including the Strait of Hormuz and Yemen, with his Pakistani counterpart, indicating that Oman is broadening its diplomatic consultations to encompass critical maritime chokepoints beyond the Red Sea. The outreach underscores Oman's traditional role as a neutral facilitator connecting Gulf and Red Sea security dialogues, potentially helping to contain further spillover from the conflict.

Rubio also addressed Houthi attacks on shipping, warning that a recent strike on a Chinese-flagged Saudi fuel vessel risks drawing China into the conflict and urged the Houthis to de-escalate. The war's official cost has reached $37.5 billion, with the administration seeking an additional $67 billion from Congress, while domestic support has eroded among Trump's base amid rising gas prices and military casualties. Diplomatic coordination also surfaced as Axios reported Mossad chief Roman Gofman held talks in Washington two weeks ago on Iran policy with CIA Director John Ratcliffe and White House officials. Reuters reported that U.S. intelligence analysts are investigating whether Russia provided targeting intelligence or upgraded drone technology to Iran, following strikes that hit CIA facilities in Riyadh and eastern Iraq. On the legislative front, the House passed an NDAA amendment blocking transgender medical procedures under TRICARE, a policy that would affect military medical facilities like Walter Reed, and separately passed a $1.15 trillion defense bill with $60 billion in additional war-related spending, heading to the Senate amid Democratic opposition over the unauthorized conflict. Declassified White House documents seeking to show Chinese election meddling instead exposed extensive Russian interference operations, Clash Report revealed. The U.S. issued a global advisory warning that diplomatic facilities, businesses, and other American institutions could face threats worldwide amid rising tensions.
